problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=4\,\text{s},$  determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)={t}^{1/3}-1,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=8\,\text{s},$ determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ({t}^{1/3}-1)\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4/3}-t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(8)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =\frac{3}{4}(8)^{4/3}-8+C \\ 4 & =12-8+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4/3}-t.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4/3}-t & =0 \\ t(\frac{3}{4}{t}^{1/3}-1) & =0 \\ t & =0,\frac{64}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t>0,$ we discard the solution $t=0.$ Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{64}{27}\,\text{s}.$
